filename: Integrated Turbulence and Machine Learning Models Explain Pier Scour in Erodible Channels.pdf
title: Integrated Turbulence and Machine Learning Models Explain Pier Scour in Erodible Channels
code_availability: Genetic programming was performed using the open-source gplearn Python library; no dedicated code repository URL is stated.
testbed_rationale: The dataset is a small tabular compilation (484 runs) of historical laboratory flume experiments for local hydraulic engineering / pier scour rather than large-scale geophysical or Earth system parameterization testbeds.
pain_points: Lack of direct fine-scale vertical velocity spectrum measurements within scour holes, requiring analogies with emergent canopy flows
Analytical intractability of full double-integration of prognostic turbulence budgets over depth and wavenumber, requiring bulk approximations and data-driven symbolic regression
Data compilation limited to laboratory-scale experiments with predominantly fine sediments (dp/H ~ 10^-4 to 10^-3)
extraction_notes: The study was supported in part by the NSF Center for Learning the Earth with Artificial Intelligence and Physics (LEAP) (Award #2019625). Symbolic regression in gplearn was configured with 5,000 population size, 20 generations, and an 80/20 train/test split.
